data.title: The Marketing Alliance authorizes repurchase of up to 800,000 shares
data.description:
The Marketing Alliance (MAAL) announced Friday the company's board of directors has authorized a share repurchase program to repurchase up to 800,000 shares of the company's issued and outstanding common stock, effective immediately and concluding March 31, 2027.

Timothy Klusas, the company's president and chief executive officer, stated, "The Board continues to believe that share repurchases are a superior way to reward shareholders. In the past, the Board felt its policy of paying dividends was not adequately reflected in the stock price.”

Source: press release

data.title: Oatly gets $4.13 per ADS cash tender offer from shareholder Verlinvest
data.description:
• Oatly Group (OTLY) announced on Friday that Verlinvest had launched a cash tender offer for all outstanding shares at $0.2065 per ordinary share, or $4.13 per ADS.

  • Verlinvest said the offer was a technical requirement under Swedish law related to its proposed buyout of China Resources' indirect stake in Oatly.

  • Oatly's independent directors are reviewing the offer and will issue a formal recommendation to shareholders by December 4, 2026.

  • The company urged shareholders not to take action until the board issues its recommendation.

data.title: Insulet downgraded at Baird on concerns over insulin pump loyalty
data.description:
• Baird downgraded Insulet (PODD) to Neutral from Overweight, citing a recent survey that found lower brand loyalty to automated insulin delivery (AID) systems than in the past. 
  • The firm cut its price target to $158 from $200 (~19% upside based on Friday's close).
  • Analyst Jeff Johnson said that Seagrove Partners' 2026 Patient Perspectives report of more than 700 people with diabetes found that individuals with an Insulet AID system had less brand loyalty than those using other companies' systems.
  • "With this lower brand loyalty, willingness to switch to alternate AID systems next year also grew, with even current Omnipod wearers voicing greater willingness than we expected to potentially switch to a competing AID system next year."
  • Johnson warned that the findings could benefit Insulet's rivals, as "only [Tandem Diabetes Care's (TNDM)] Mobi Tubeless and [MiniMed's (MMED)] Fit check both these 'tighter algo' and '7-day wear potential' boxes, with Mobi-T fitting this latter point better than Fit, in our view."

data.description:

The decline coincided with a pullback across chip stocks. Peers AMAT, LRCX and MU fell almost 11%, almost 10% and 14%, respectively, while the XLK technology sector ETF dropped more than 7%.

data.title: Nasdaq plunges 10% for the week after Friday's bloodbath
data.description:
A continued weakness in tech stocks sent the Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) spiralling on Friday, with the index plummeting 5.28% to close at 22,617.73 points.

The tech-heavy index registered significant losses for the second session in a row after declining 2.25% on Thursday. In addition, the highly anticipated IPO of AI startup Anthropic (ANT) failed to impress investors, with the stock down over 20% since its market debut.

For the week, Nasdaq lost 10%.

The top five detractors for the week comprised mostly tech names, led by Strategy (MSTR) for the second week in a row. Shares of the bitcoin treasury company plunged after the world’s largest cryptocurrency sank to under $65K on Monday.

Nebius Group (NBIS) and Sandisk (SNDK) were among the worst hit during the week’s tech selloff.

Only four companies floated in the green territory this week, with Palo Alto Networks (PANW) leading the gains on the back of strong quarterly results and guidance and its $4.5B acquisition of startup Applied Compute.

data.title: WeRide targets 2026 revenue of at least RMB 1.1B while projecting positive quarterly free cash flow in 2028
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: WeRide (WRD) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Xu Han framed the quarter as outperformance on growth and losses, saying, "Our revenue grew by 88% year-over-year to RMB 321.5 million and the gross margin improved to 43%" and "our net loss narrowed by 22.6% to RMB 310 million." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Xu Han)
  • CEO Han emphasized Robotaxi international traction, stating, "Our Robotaxi revenue grew by 204% year-over-year, of which 90% comes from overseas market" and "Currently, WeRide is Uber's largest fully driverless Robotaxi partner outside the U.S." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • CEO Han highlighted scale and unit economics signals, including, "our L4 fleet reached about 4,100 vehicles and our Robotaxi fleet has surpassed 2,300 vehicles" and "In China, we achieved positive unit economics per Robotaxi in Guangzhou." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • CEO Han detailed geographic milestones, saying, "In Europe, we received Spain's first national operating permit for L4 autonomous passenger vehicles, and we expect to launch commercial operations by year-end" and "we are on track toward our goal of deploying tens of thousands of Robotaxis in Europe before 2030." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • CFO Xuan Li summarized the quarter in three points: "Revenue grew 88% year-over-year to a record RMB 321.5 million," "Gross margin reached 43%," and "Net loss narrowed 22.6% quarter-over-quarter to RMB 310 million." (CFO & Head of International Xuan Li)
  • CFO Li addressed capital actions and dilution risk directly: "Since March, we have repurchased over USD 95 million of our shares" and "With our plans fully funded, we see no reason to issue new shares at a valuation that we believe does not reflect the value of this company." (CFO & Head of International Li)

Outlook

  • CFO Li raised full-year revenue expectations, stating, "Given our strong result this quarter, we now expect 2026 revenue of at least RMB 1.1 billion" and tied forward growth to deployment, saying, "overseas fleet that we expect to double" and "L2++ delivery growing towards 500,000 units." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • CFO Li guided to lower cash burn and defined free-cash-flow targets: "we expect total cash burn to drop to about RMB 1 billion in 2027" and "We remain on track for our first quarter of positive free cash flow in 2028 and positive free cash flow for the full year in 2029." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Versus the prior quarter’s messaging, Q3 added a more explicit capital return and issuance stance, with CFO Li saying, "we have repurchased over USD 95 million of our shares" and "we see no reason to issue new shares." (CFO & Head of International Li)

Financial Results

  • CFO Li reported revenue and mix: "The total revenue reached a record RMB 321.5 million" and "Overseas revenue grew 171.5% to RMB 146.9 million." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • CFO Li described margin drivers and variability: "Gross margin reached 43% this quarter" and "this quarter's gross margin also benefit from a favorable revenue mix, which may vary from quarter to quarter." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • CFO Li detailed segment performance without quantifying every line item repeatedly, noting, "L4 revenue grew 47.2% year-over-year to RMB 168.8 million" and "AI infrastructure revenue nearly doubled." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • CFO Li explained a notable G&A swing: "Administrative expense were RMB 13.9 million this quarter" and "This includes a noncash reversal of about RMB 49 million in share-based compensation expenses related to employee departures." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • CFO Li reconciled cash movement and implied near-term stabilization: "Our cash and cash equivalents fell by RMB 1.67 billion" but "in total, our cash reserve declined by about RMB 700 million" and "we expect our total cash reserves to remain stable in the fourth quarter." (CFO & Head of International Li)

Q&A

  • Paul Gong, UBS Investment Bank: asked about fleet scalability versus "Waymo and Tesla" and competition in Europe; Founder, Chairman & CEO Han replied, "we have our competitive edge" and cited "our L4 system combines a one-stage end-to-end model with dedicated safety architecture" plus "we got the Spain's first national L4 operating permit." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • Tim Hsiao, Morgan Stanley: asked what must happen for overseas deployment to accelerate; CFO Li said scaling is often gated by permitting, adding, "our main constraint is not really the tech, but it's really just the permit timing" and disclosed, "We have binding contracts for about 3,000 Robotaxis globally as of today." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Jiajie Shen, JPMorgan: asked about expanding profitable L4 operations in China and global expansion plans; Founder, Chairman & CEO Han said, "Guangzhou achieved a positive UE at the city level for a full quarter for the first time" and reiterated the scaling guardrail: "our priority is positive unit economics, healthy cash flow and first sustainable operations." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • Ming-Hsun Lee, BofA Securities: asked about Uber partnership plans; Founder, Chairman & CEO Han said, "Uber is definitely our core strategic partner and a major shareholder" and "we expect to launch in several more European cities next year." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • Ming-Hsun Lee, BofA Securities: asked whether general-purpose AI could solve autonomous driving; Founder, Chairman & CEO Han responded, "controlling a car is a completely different problem" and "within 5 years, if you look at our plan, we have already deployed our Robotaxi fleet to cover the global market." CFO Li added, "WeRide has spent years to build" and "we have permitted in nine countries." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han; CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Yuqian Ding, HSBC: asked about L2++ competition, pricing pressure, and orders; Founder, Chairman & CEO Han said, "the competition is kind of intensive" but argued, "our cost is significantly lower than our peers" and cited demand ambition: "I look forward to take even larger market share in ADAS market." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • Yiran Tao: asked for a precise definition of unit economics; CFO Li said, "I'll be very precise about what it includes" and listed costs including "vehicle depreciation," "insurance," and "telecom fees," adding, "slightly less than half of the total cost goes to like it's vehicle depreciation related." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Dongbing Han, Huatai Securities: asked about cash runway to breakeven and share issuance; CFO Li answered, "yes, we have enough cash to reach breakeven in 2029" and "we will not carry equity issuance of placement at the current valuation." (CFO & Head of International Li)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing around competitive threats and dependencies, with UBS explicitly asking for comparisons "versus the global leaders like Waymo and Tesla" and HSBC highlighting that "competition is getting intense" and "more pressure on pricing." (Paul Gong, UBS Investment Bank; Yuqian Ding, HSBC)
  • Management’s prepared remarks were positive and assertive, with CEO Han opening, "We delivered a very strong quarter" and CFO Li saying results were "well ahead of street expectations," while Q&A answers stayed confident and occasionally defensive on moat-building, including, "we have our competitive edge" and "our main constraint is not really the tech." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han; CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Compared with Q2’s emphasis on an "inflection point" and model repeatability, Q3 added sharper investor-facing positioning on dilution and buybacks, including, "we have repurchased over USD 95 million" and "we see no reason to issue new shares." (CFO & Head of International Li)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Management kept the same strategic pillars—asset-light scaling and overseas acceleration—but Q3 elevated Europe regulatory progress with "Spain's first national operating permit" and set a nearer-term milestone: "commercial operations by year-end." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)
  • Q3 introduced clearer capital allocation signaling than Q2, with explicit buyback disclosure and issuance stance: "repurchased over USD 95 million" and "no reason to issue new shares." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Financially, Q3 reported a higher gross margin than Q2’s "37.5%" level and a lower net loss than Q2’s "RMB 401 million," alongside a lower cash balance versus Q2’s "RMB 5.4 billion"; management emphasized the Q3 cash movement was "timing, not run rate burn." (CFO & Head of International Li; CFO & Head of International Li (Q2))
  • Analyst focus shifted from Q2’s platform-dependence concerns toward direct competitive framing against Waymo/Tesla and Europe crowding, while still revisiting dilution/cash runway. (Paul Gong, UBS Investment Bank; Dongbing Han, Huatai Securities)

Risks and Concerns

  • Permitting and regulatory timing remained a central gating factor, with CFO Li stating, "our main constraint is not really the tech, but it's really just the permit timing," while management’s mitigation centered on regulatory engagement and track record, including, "industry-leading safety record overseas." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Gross margin durability was flagged as mix-sensitive, with CFO Li cautioning, "this quarter's gross margin also benefit from a favorable revenue mix, which may vary from quarter to quarter." (CFO & Head of International Li)
  • Competitive pressure was acknowledged in L2++/L3, with CEO Han saying, "the competition is kind of intensive" and positioning response as lower cost and shared technology with L4: "our one-stage end-to-end solution" and "shares the technology we developed with our L4 driverless operation." (Founder, Chairman & CEO Han)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a record revenue quarter with a higher gross margin and a narrower net loss, while emphasizing that overseas Robotaxi service fees and an asset-light model are driving recurring revenue. Leadership highlighted regulatory progress in Europe, positive unit economics in Guangzhou, and disclosed share repurchases alongside a stated intent not to issue equity at current valuations. Forward targets centered on 2026 revenue of at least RMB 1.1 billion, lower cash burn in 2027, and a first positive quarterly free cash flow in 2028, with permitting timelines repeatedly cited as the key constraint on deployment acceleration.

data.title: Broadcom sinks 12% as Google trims 2027 TPU orders, tech stocks drop
data.description:
Semiconductor and software company Broadcom (AVGO) slumped just over 12% today after a report that Google trimmed its planned 2027 orders for Broadcom-designed TPU chips. The stock finished at $304.65, a drop of $42 on the day.

Google reportedly reduced planned 2027 shipments of Broadcom-designed TPU 8i chips by about 1 million units, or roughly 20%. At the same time, it increased planned orders for MediaTek-designed TPU 8t chips. The report described the shift as a response to compute allocation and data-center power constraints.

The retreat also coincided with a general selloff in tech stocks. The Nasdaq fell more than 5% during the session.
